Canada immigration pathways

Canada offers more than a visitor visa. Below are the main immigration, family, study and work routes listed by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) — including the government fee for each route. Fees are IRCC fees only and can change; we check the current program page before advising on your case.

Skilled workers — permanent residence

Permanent residence for skilled workers.

Express Entry

The main route. Covers three programs: Federal Skilled Worker, Federal Skilled Trades, and Canadian Experience Class. You need qualifying skilled work experience and English or French.

Fee from CAN$1,590

Provincial Nominee Program (PNP)

A province or territory nominates you for its own labour needs. You need the nomination, plus the work experience and education that province asks for.

Fee from CAN$1,590

Province and community programs — permanent residence

Permanent residence through a province, region or community program.

Atlantic Immigration Program

For skilled workers and international graduates settling in New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island, or Newfoundland and Labrador. Needs a job offer from a designated employer and 1 year of work experience (unless you studied there).

Fee from CAN$1,590

Rural Community Immigration Pilot

Skilled workers for smaller communities. Needs a job offer from a designated employer and 1 year of qualifying work experience in the last 3 years.

Fee from CAN$1,590

Francophone Community Immigration Pilot

French-speaking skilled workers for smaller Francophone communities outside Quebec. Needs a job offer, 1 year of work experience, and French.

Fee from CAN$1,590

Home Care Worker Immigration pilots

For home child care and home support workers. Needs a job offer in that work, plus qualifying experience or relevant training.

Fee from CAN$1,590

Quebec — permanent residence

Permanent residence through Quebec.

Quebec selected skilled workers

For people holding a Quebec Selection Certificate.

Fee from CAN$1,590

Quebec entrepreneurs and investors

For Certificate holders with enough money to settle.

Fee from CAN$2,495

Family sponsorship — permanent residence

Permanent residence through sponsorship by family in Canada.

Spouse or partner

Sponsor must be 18+, living in Canada, and a citizen, permanent resident, or registered Indian.

From CAN$1,260

Child

Sponsorship of a child.

CAN$180 per child

Parents or grandparents

Sponsor must show enough income to support them.

From CAN$1,260

Adopted child and other relatives

For adoption and other eligible relatives.

From CAN$180 per child for adoption · From CAN$1,260 for other eligible relatives

Study and work — temporary routes that can lead to permanent residence

Temporary routes that can lead to permanent residence.

Study permit

Must enrol at a designated learning institution and show enough money for tuition and living.

From CAN$150

Post-graduation work permit

For recent graduates of a full-time program of at least 8 months at an eligible institution.

CAN$255

Work permit

Employer-specific and open work permits.

From CAN$155 for an employer-specific permit · From CAN$255 for an open permit

International Experience Canada

For youth aged 18 to 35 from participating countries: Working Holiday, Young Professionals, or Co-op.

From CAN$185

Visiting only

For visits — these routes do not lead to permanent residence on their own.

Parent and grandparent super visa

Visit children or grandchildren for up to 5 years at a time. Needs an invitation letter and health insurance.

From CAN$100

Visit Canada

Tourist, business, or transit visa, or an eTA.

Source: IRCC — Explore immigration programs. Processing times vary by program and country, so check the program page before quoting a timeline to a client.

About Good Luck Visa Consultants

Good Luck Visa Consultants is a visa consultancy based in Rosettenville, Johannesburg, helping clients across South Africa and worldwide prepare tourist and student visa applications.

A visa is decided on your documents and your credibility. Our work is the careful part: checking that your application form, cover letter, bookings, bank statements and travel plan are complete, consistent and honest — and that everything is submitted through the official channel for your destination.

We work remotely, over WhatsApp and email, and we are open 24 hours, every day. If your destination isn't one of the 19 we cover in depth, message us anyway — we will tell you honestly whether we can help.

How we work — honestly

  • No approval guarantee. Only the embassy or consulate decides. Anyone who promises you a visa is not being straight with you.
  • Honest from the start. If your case is weak, we say so before you spend money on embassy fees.
  • Everything declared. Previous refusals and travel history are handled openly, the right way.
  • Official channels only. Applications go through the real government or authorised centre for your destination — never a lookalike site.
  • Matched documents. Your cover letter, bookings, statements and plan all tell the same story.

Frequently asked questions

Straight answers to the questions clients ask us most.

Can you guarantee my visa will be approved?

No — and be careful of anyone who does. Only the embassy or consulate decides. Our job is to make sure your file is complete, consistent and honest, which gives your genuine application its best chance.

How do I start?

Message us on WhatsApp with your destination and your intended travel dates. We'll reply with the next step and the documents to start gathering. No office visit is needed.

Which destinations do you cover?

We prepare files for 19 destinations: Albania, France, Germany, Belgium, Luxembourg, the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada, Australia, Japan, the United Arab Emirates, Türkiye, India, Thailand, China, South Africa, New Zealand, Vietnam and Egypt. See the destinations section above for the official route for each one.

I was refused before. Can you still help?

Yes. Send us your refusal letter if you have it. We'll go through the reasons with you, tell you honestly what has changed or can be improved, and whether — and when — it makes sense to apply again. Previous refusals must always be declared in future applications.

Do you help with student visas?

Yes — student visas are one of our two main services, alongside tourist and visitor visas. We help organise your admission, funding and supporting documents into a complete file, in the order the embassy expects.

How early should I start?

As early as you can. Appointment slots fill up — for some destinations, new slots only open on certain days — and gathering bank statements, letters and bookings takes time. The sooner we see your dates, the sooner we can plan your file and your booking around them.

Where do I submit my application?

Always through the official channel for your destination — the government portal, embassy, or its authorised application centre (for example TLScontact for Belgium and Luxembourg in South Africa). We show you the official link for your destination and guide you through it; we never use lookalike or unofficial sites.

What does your help cost?

It depends on the service and your case. Message us with your destination and visa type and we'll confirm the fee for your file before any work starts — no surprises. Embassy and application-centre fees are separate and are paid by you directly through the official channel.

Do I need to visit your office?

No. We are based in Rosettenville, Johannesburg, but almost everything is done over WhatsApp and email, so we help clients across South Africa and worldwide. We are open 24 hours, every day.
